# CLAUDE.md — travel-assist

## Critical Commands

Claude must use **only** these commands. Never invent alternatives (e.g., `mvn`, `npm`, `kotlin`, direct `java` invocations):

```bash
# Install / resolve dependencies
./gradlew dependencies

# Build the project (compiles Kotlin, runs tests, packages JAR)
./gradlew build

# Run tests only
./gradlew test

# Start the application locally
./gradlew bootRun
```

> **Never** use `gradle` (without the wrapper) — always use `./gradlew` to ensure the correct Gradle version is used.

---

## Always Do

1. **Always place new controllers in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/controller/`**, new services in `.../service/`, new repositories in `.../repository/`, new entities in `.../model/`, and new DTOs in `.../dto/`. The module layout is strictly enforced by convention.

2. **Always run `./gradlew test` after changing any class in `TripController`, `TripService`, `TripRepository`, `Trip`, or `TripDto`** — these are the core CRUD pipeline and any breakage must be caught immediately.

3. **Always use `@field:` annotation use-site targets in Kotlin DTOs** (e.g., `@field:NotBlank` in `TripDto.kt`). Omitting `field:` places the annotation on the constructor parameter, silently breaking Jakarta Bean Validation at runtime.

4. **Always use `var` fields (not `val`) on the `Trip` JPA entity in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/model/Trip.kt`**, consistent with the existing entity design. JPA requires mutable fields for proxying and dirty-checking.

5. **Always add new dependencies to `build.gradle.kts`** — this is the single source of truth for the build. Never attempt to add JARs manually or edit generated lock files.

6. **Always check for an existing `application.properties` AND `application.yml` conflict** in `src/main/resources/` when adding new configuration — both files are loaded by Spring Boot and one may silently override the other. Prefer consolidating into one file unless explicitly instructed otherwise.

7. **Always write or update a corresponding test in `src/test/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/`** when adding or modifying any method in `TripService` or any endpoint in `TripController`. Never leave new logic untested.

8. **Always use camelCase** for all Kotlin identifiers (variables, functions, parameters) and PascalCase for class names, consistent with the existing naming convention across this codebase.

## Never Do

1. **Never modify or delete Gradle wrapper files**: `gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`, `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar`, or `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties`. These are pinned for reproducible builds.

2. **Never edit CI/CD workflow files** under `.github/workflows/` — specifically `agentic-ready.yml` and `context-refresh.yml`. These are managed externally.

3. **Never modify `settings.gradle.kts`** — the project name and structure are fixed. Changing this can break CI and all wrapper-relative paths.

4. **Never add secrets, API keys, passwords, or credentials** to any source file, `application.properties`, `application.yml`, or any file tracked by Git.

5. **Never invoke the DGS `generateJava` task** unless a GraphQL schema file has been added under `src/main/resources/graphql-client/`. No schema files currently exist — invoking this task will fail the build.

6. **Never switch the persistence layer from H2** (in-memory) to a production database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc.) without explicit user instruction. The current H2 setup in `application.properties`/`application.yml` is intentional for local development.

7. **Never delete existing test files** in `src/test/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/` without providing a direct replacement. Test coverage must not regress.

8. **Never assume GraalVM native image compilation is safe** for new features added without testing. The `nativeCompile` task has strict constraints on reflection and dynamic proxies — newly added beans or reflection-heavy code may require native hints.

## Architecture Notes

1. **Strict Controller → Service → Repository layering.** HTTP requests enter at `TripController` (`/api/trips`), business logic lives exclusively in `TripService`, and all database access goes through `TripRepository`. Do not place database queries in controllers or business logic in repositories.

2. **Spring Modulith is active** — the package structure under `com.vb.nattamai.travelassist` is expected to eventually form explicit modules. Keep `controller`, `service`, `repository`, `model`, and `dto` as separate packages and avoid cross-package direct field access or circular dependencies between them.

3. **H2 in-memory database is the only persistence target.** `TripRepository` extends Spring Data JPA and relies on H2 for both local runs (`./gradlew bootRun`) and tests (`./gradlew test`). The schema is auto-managed by JPA (`ddl-auto`). There is no Flyway or Liquibase migration layer — schema changes are reflected by modifying the `Trip` entity directly.

4. **Spring Boot 4.0.4 is bleeding-edge.** Not all third-party libraries are guaranteed to be compatible. Before adding any new dependency, verify it supports Spring Boot 4.x / Spring Framework 7.x. This especially applies to Spring Security, Spring Cloud, and any community starters.

## Domain Context

| Concept | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Trip** | The single core domain entity (`model/Trip.kt`), persisted in the `trips` table. Attributes include `id` (auto-generated), `title`, `description`, `destination`, and date range fields. This is the only entity in the system currently. |
| **TripDto** | The inbound API contract (`dto/TripDto.kt`) used for both create and update requests. It is **not** the same as `Trip` — it carries Jakarta validation constraints (`@field:NotBlank` on `title`) and is mapped to/from `Trip` in `TripService`. |
| **TripService** | The transactional boundary (`service/TripService.kt`). All `@Transactional` annotations belong here. It maps between `TripDto` and `Trip`, enforces business rules, and delegates persistence to `TripRepository`. |
| **TripRepository** | A pure Spring Data JPA interface (`repository/TripRepository.kt`). It extends a Spring Data base interface and provides zero-boilerplate CRUD. Custom queries (JPQL or native) should be added here as named methods or `@Query` annotations. |
| **TripController** | The HTTP adapter (`controller/TripController.kt`) exposing `GET /api/trips`, `GET /api/trips/{id}`, `POST /api/trips`, `PUT /api/trips/{id}`, and `DELETE /api/trips/{id}`. It receives `TripDto`, delegates to `TripService`, and returns appropriate HTTP responses. |

## After Every Change

Complete this checklist **in order** before considering any change done:

- [ ] **Run tests:** `./gradlew test` — all tests must pass with zero failures or errors.
- [ ] **Run full build:** `./gradlew build` — ensures compilation, tests, and packaging all succeed together.
- [ ] **Verify no dual-config conflict:** If you touched `src/main/resources/application.properties` or `src/main/resources/application.yml`, confirm the two files do not define the same key with conflicting values.
- [ ] **Check annotation use-site targets:** If you added or modified any DTO under `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/dto/`, confirm all validation annotations use `@field:` prefix (e.g., `@field:NotBlank`, `@field:NotNull`).
- [ ] **Confirm no restricted files were touched:** Verify `gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`, `gradle/wrapper/*`, `settings.gradle.kts`, and `.github/workflows/*` are **unchanged** (`git diff --name-only` is a reliable check).
- [ ] **Confirm test coverage:** If a new method was added to `TripService` or a new endpoint to `TripController`, a corresponding test exists in `src/test/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/`.
- [ ] **If DGS codegen is involved:** Only run `./gradlew generateJava` if a `.graphqls` schema file exists under `src/main/resources/graphql-client/`. Otherwise, skip this task explicitly.
